About

I am a Master of Engineering student in Geomatics and Land Survey at the National Advanced School of Public Works (ENSTP) in Yaoundé, Cameroon, with my thesis defense pending. My work combines remote sensing, GIS database development, and GNSS field surveying, so I understand data from the moment it is collected to the final map.

I am looking for internship and entry-level opportunities across geomatics engineering, including geospatial data analysis, GIS, remote sensing, photogrammetry, and land surveying, where I can apply spatial data to real development questions such as trade corridors, infrastructure, and land use. I speak English and French natively.

Projects

Spatial Analysis of Touristic Areas in Cameroon: Case of Mount Cameroon

ENSTP Mini-Project, 2026 · Supervisor: Dr. Eric Zangue

Cameroon's tourist areas are rarely studied with spatial methods, which makes planning difficult. I mapped the Mount Cameroon and Buea area with free Landsat imagery to show how the territory is organised and where planning should focus.

2Landsat sensors (8 & 9)
4spatial analyses
3distinct zones found
Forest core
Agricultural transition
Urban gateway

The three zones identified around Mount Cameroon (schematic, not to scale).

Land cover

Classified forest, built-up, bare volcanic ground, and water, then checked against an earlier land cover map.

NDVI

Mapped vegetation density to locate the ecologically valuable zones that support ecotourism.

NDBI

Mapped built-up areas and road corridors, showing where urban growth presses on natural areas.

Land surface emissivity

Derived from NDVI and thermal Band 10 to compare the thermal conditions of forest and urban areas.

What I found and recommended

  • NDVI and NDBI showed the expected inverse relationship, which supports the consistency of the results.
  • The three-zone structure suggests tourism circuits that link the urban gateway, cultural villages, and the mountain park.
  • Recommended zoning to protect forest zones, infrastructure development focused on already built-up areas, and GIS-based planning by national and local authorities.

Drone Photogrammetry at ENSTP: PPK and Ground Control Surveys

Photogrammetry lab project, ENSTP Yaoundé, 2026

I processed two separate drone surveys of the ENSTP area to produce orthomosaics and surface models at centimetre resolution. One was georeferenced with PPK GNSS and no ground control, the other with ground control points, each with its own flight, camera, and coverage.

Survey 1: PPK georeferencing (no GCPs)

DJI Matrice 4E · processed in Pix4D
665images, 100% calibrated
1.94 cmground sampling distance
23.2 haarea mapped
0.167 pxmean reprojection error

Orthomosaic (left) and DSM (right), PPK survey. Tap to enlarge.

  • Base GNSS receiver on the known ENSTP control point E01, with raw rover observations and the image event file recorded during the flight.
  • Post-processed in Emlid Studio (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, SBAS) in WGS 84 / UTM 32N, then geotagged the images.
  • Mean absolute camera position uncertainty of about 3 mm per axis, image geolocation RMS of 1.6 mm (X), 2.6 mm (Y) and 3.2 cm (Z), and about 78 million densified points.

Survey 2: Ground control survey

Separate flight and camera (FC6310) · processed with ground control points in Metashape
619images, 100% calibrated
1.37 cmground sampling distance
8.2 haarea mapped
0.120 pxmean reprojection error

Orthomosaic (left) and DSM (right), ground control survey. Tap to enlarge.

  • Ground control points measured with GNSS and introduced into the processing to tie the model to the ground and reduce global deformation.
  • Dense reconstruction of about 56 million points at an average density of roughly 1,230 points per cubic metre, with DSM and orthomosaic at 1.37 cm per pixel.
  • Stable camera calibration, with only 0.09% change between initial and optimised internal parameters.
